content: 1. The Xpert Ultra test demonstrates high certainty of evidence when used in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) as an initial diagnostic tool for tuberculosis (TB) meningitis. 2. The Xpert MTB/RIF test is recommended as the initial diagnostic test for extrapulmonary TB when applied to specimens such as lymph node aspirates, lymph node biopsies, pleural fluid, peritoneal fluid, pericardial fluid, synovial fluid, or urine. 3. The Xpert Ultra test is recommended as the initial diagnostic test for extrapulmonary TB when used on lymph node aspirates or lymph node biopsy specimens. 4. The Xpert Ultra test is also recommended for detecting rifampicin resistance in both adults and children who present with signs and symptoms of extrapulmonary TB. 5. The Xpert MTB/RIF test can be used in blood samples for diagnosing disseminated TB. 6. The Xpert MTB/RIF assay is validated for diagnosing both pulmonary and extrapulmonary TB in adults and children. 7. Molecular assays, such as Xpert MTB/RIF and Xpert Ultra, are intended as initial diagnostic tests for pulmonary and extrapulmonary TB, as well as for detecting rifampicin resistance in adults and children. 8. In adults with pulmonary TB symptoms and an initial Xpert Ultra trace-positive result, repeated testing with Ultra is not recommended due to very low certainty of evidence regarding test accuracy. 9. In children with pulmonary TB symptoms in settings with a pretest probability below 5% and an initial Xpert MTB/RIF negative result, repeated testing with Xpert MTB/RIF using sputum, gastric fluid, nasopharyngeal aspirate, or stool specimens is not recommended due to low or very low certainty of evidence for test accuracy. 10. In children with pulmonary TB symptoms in settings with a pretest probability of 5% or more and an initial Xpert MTB/RIF negative result, repeated testing with Xpert MTB/RIF (up to two tests) using sputum, gastric fluid, nasopharyngeal aspirate, or stool specimens may be considered, though evidence certainty remains low or very low. 11. In children with pulmonary TB symptoms in settings with a pretest probability below 5% and an initial Xpert Ultra negative result, repeated testing with Xpert Ultra using sputum or nasopharyngeal aspirate specimens is not recommended due to very low certainty of evidence for test accuracy. 12. Repeated Xpert Ultra testing is not recommended in adults with an initial Xpert Ultra trace-positive result. 13. Repeated Xpert MTB/RIF testing is not recommended in children in low-prevalence settings. 14. Repeated Xpert MTB/RIF testing is recommended in children in high-prevalence settings using sputum, gastric fluid, nasopharyngeal aspirate, or stool specimens. 15. Repeated Xpert Ultra testing is recommended in children in both lowand high-prevalence settings using sputum and nasopharyngeal aspirate specimens. 16. The WHO guidelines recommend the use of Xpert MTB/RIF or Xpert Ultra as initial diagnostic tests for pulmonary TB in adults with TB symptoms or chest radiographic abnormalities, replacing culture in these cases. This recommendation is conditional, with low certainty of evidence for Xpert MTB/RIF and moderate certainty for Xpert Ultra. 17. The TrueNat MTB, MTB Plus, and MTB-RIF Dx assays, developed in India, are molecular diagnostic tools that can be used at the same health system level as Xpert MTB/RIF. TrueNat MTB and MTB Plus are used as initial diagnostic tests for TB, while MTB-RIF Dx is a reflex test for detecting rifampicin resistance in positive cases. 18. TrueNat assays utilize real-time micro-PCR technology to detect Mycobacterium tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance in DNA extracted from sputum specimens. These assays are battery-operated, automated, and designed for use in peripheral laboratories with minimal infrastructure and training requirements. 19. TrueNat MTB or MTB Plus may be used as initial diagnostic tests for pulmonary TB in adults and children, replacing smear microscopy or culture. This is a conditional recommendation with moderate certainty of evidence for test accuracy. 20. TrueNat MTB-RIF Dx may be used as an initial test for rifampicin resistance in adults and children with positive TrueNat MTB or MTB Plus results, replacing culture and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence for test accuracy. 21. The diagnostic performance of TrueNat assays has been evaluated in microscopy centers in India, but further assessment of operational characteristics and acceptability in intended settings is required to confirm assay performance. 22. The WHO guidelines emphasize the need for further evidence on the use of TrueNat assays in people living with HIV (PLHIV) and in children, as data on test accuracy in these populations are limited or indirect. 23. The TrueNat MTB-RIF Dx assay applies a reflex (two-step) testing approach for rifampicin resistance, and its recommendation is only applicable to patients with positive TrueNat MTB or MTB Plus results. 24. The diagnostic accuracy of TrueNat MTB, MTB Plus, and MTB-RIF Dx assays has been assessed through multicenter international evaluations conducted by FIND, with comparisons made to Xpert MTB/RIF or Xpert Ultra in reference laboratories. 25. The certainty of evidence for TrueNat MTB and MTB Plus assays is low for sensitivity but high for specificity. For TrueNat MTB-RIF Dx, concerns about imprecision and inconsistency in sensitivity estimates were noted, with evidence certainty rated as low for sensitivity and high for specificity.
